title: Cue Concision Steward Notes
content:
Purpose:
- Short personal scratchpad to iterate on a small suite of prompts and diagnostics focused on "conciseness stewardship" (getting models to be reliably concise without losing required facts).
- Keep examples lightweight so I can run quick A/Bs in the playground and ingest into the prompt-registry later.

Guiding constraints (why this exists):
- Product teams want answers that are short, actionable, and cite the minimal context.
- Long-winded outputs increase token costs and surface hallucination risk.
- Need solid few-shot + template combos that bias for brevity across model families.

Immediate goals:
1) Create 3 template families that produce <= 120 tokens on average for FAQ-style answers while preserving completeness.
2) Document 6 failure modes and quick detection heuristics.
3) Produce a tiny eval harness (20 prompts) with expected outputs and a simple pass/fail rubric.

Template family A: "Concise Instruction + Must-Haves" (best for single-question answers)
- Prompt skeleton: "You are a concise assistant. Answer in 1–3 short sentences. Always include: [must-have], then a one-line suggestion if applicable. If the question is ambiguous, ask one clarifying yes/no question. Do not produce examples unless asked."
- Few-shot (2-shot):
  Q: "How do I reset my API key?"
  A: "Go to Settings → API keys, click 'Rotate', copy new key. Revoke the old key if compromised."

  Q: "What causes high latency in inference?"
  A: "Common causes: undersized GPUs, small batch sizes, and synchronous requests. Check GPU util and tail latency logs."

- Variations to try: add token ceilings, append "Prefer active voice", or add explicit "Do not include background history."

Template family B: "Checklist + One-liner" (good for operational advice)
- Prompt skeleton: "Provide a 3-item checklist (bulleted), followed by a single-sentence recommended next action. Keep bullets <12 words each."
- Few-shot:
  Q: "How to reduce memory usage for LLM serving?"
  A: "- Use quantized weights
- Enable KV cache eviction for long contexts
- Batch requests with a 50ms window
Recommendation: Try 4-bit quantization on a staging cluster and compare p50 latency."

Template family C: "Constraint-first Rewriter" (for user-generated long answers)
- Skeleton: "Rewrite the following reply to be no more than X tokens, preserve factual assertions, remove repetition, and keep the same meaning. If facts are missing, add a single-sentence clarification prefixed with 'Note:'."
- Use-case: partner support messages, community responses.

Failure modes observed (catalog):
1) Semantic pruning: model removes qualifiers and changes meaning when compressing.
   Heuristic: compare named entity counts and relations between orig and compressed output. If entity count drops, flag.
2) Hallucinated brevity: adds concise but incorrect steps.
   Heuristic: run a fact-checker prompt or a knowledge lookup on any step with a proper noun.
3) Politeness bloat: model turns concise answers into polite-but-long replies.
   Heuristic: detect opening/closing salutations > 8 tokens and trim.
4) Ambiguity fallback: model chooses an interpretation and deletes alternatives.
   Heuristic: prompt should force explicit clarification if ambiguity detected; otherwise flag for human review.
5) Token-ceiling blowouts: model ignores token limit in few-shot variants.
   Heuristic: prepend explicit token budget and use a countdown token estimator in eval harness.
6) List explosion: converts single-line recommendations into multi-paragraph examples.
   Heuristic: count newline segments; enforce bullet-only format in instruction.

Small eval harness (20 prompts sketch):
- 8 FAQ-style (single fact or step)
- 6 operational checklists (requires 2–3 bullets)
- 6 rewrite/compression cases (original long reply + desired token cap)
For each: expected_properties: [complete_facts, <=120 tokens, no salutations, no examples unless asked].
Scoring (manual for now): pass/fail + reason (loss of fact / >tokens / added examples / changed meaning).

Quick experiments to run (next 2 sprints):
- Sprint 1: Run Template A vs Template B on 30 FAQ prompts across 3 models (small/medium/large). Record p50 token usage and pass rate.
- Sprint 2: Use Template C to compress 50 actual support replies (synthetic redacted dataset) and measure semantic-similarity (BLEU + entailment check).

Micro-experiments (fast checks):
- Add a preface: "Answer in English. Do not include backstory." vs nothing — measure difference in token usage.
- Compare explicit token budget line: "Limit answer to 50 tokens." vs soft: "Answer briefly."

Example few-shot set (compact):
- Shot 1
  Q: "Where do I find the logs for request failures?"
  A: "Logs: Console → Observability → Request logs. Filter by request_id or error code. If unclear, attach request_id to ticket."
- Shot 2
  Q: "How to enable private deployment?"
  A: "Open Console → Deployments → New private. Pick VPC, attach KMS. Request support for on-prem package."
- Shot 3 (compression example)
  Orig: "We typically recommend rotating keys every 90 days to reduce impact of leaks; if you have automation that will rotate too frequently it might interrupt long-running jobs; ensure you plan downtime windows."
  Compressed (desired): "Rotate keys every 90 days. Coordinate rotations to avoid disrupting long jobs."

Operational checklist (quick copy for SLA page drafts):
- Keep answers under 120 tokens unless detailed step-by-step requested.
- Always return a suggested next action (1 sentence) when recommending changes.
- Do not include sign-offs or emojis.

Notes to self / todo:
- Build small sandbox harness that records token_count, entities_changed, and entailment_score. Tie to playground for rapid replays.
- Add these templates to prompt-registry under namespace devx/concise once stable.
- Ask SRE (Leo) for 10 real-world support replies (sanitized) to test Template C.
- Run a per-model calibration to see which families reliably obey token ceilings (LLama2-13B, Redstone-34B, etc.).

References and useful tickets:
- ENG-1234 (investigate token bloat in support answers)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-registry/pull/412 (seeded few-shot harness)
- Slack: #devx thread 8921 (user complaints about long answers)

Random thoughts / heuristics to keep:
- If model writes more than 3 clauses per sentence, prefer rewriting to two sentences max.
- For checklists, enforce parallel structure: verbs first.
- Consider a "compression guard" chain: compress -> fact-check -> rephrase minimal if fact-check fails.

End of scratchpad. Will iterate.
